predictions.experiment: Pooled within-problem concordance of length with wrongness for the cued base: over all (right, wrong) pairs of finished attempt-0 samples of the same problem, the fraction in which the wrong sample has more new tokens.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows whose score_v3 is null/missing. Group by problem_index. Within each problem, form every pair (i, j) with score_v3_i == 1 and score_v3_j == 0. Pair value: 1 if n_new_j > n_new_i, 0.5 if n_new_j == n_new_i, 0 otherwise. Statistic = sum of pair values over all problems / total number of pairs over all problems. Problems with no such pair contribute nothing. Cap-hit rows and later attempts are not used.
predictions.note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (committed; read in place, else copied from git HEAD into runs/theory-tests/). 2,000 attempt-0 rows, no duplicate (problem, sample, attempt) keys; score_v3 is int 0/1 on every row, cap_hit is bool, so the null-score drop removes nothing. Main: ties = 0.5 as the recipe says. Ambiguity: the experiment text says 'fraction in which the wrong sample has more new tokens', i.e. ties = 0; that is alt_measured (ties in n_new are rare, so the two should be close). Pooled over pairs, so problems with 2 right / 2 wrong weigh 4 pairs and 3/1 weigh 3; an unweighted per-problem mean would differ and is not computed. Cap hits are excluded before pairing, so a problem whose only wrong samples are cap hits contributes no pairs. refuted_by: measured < 0.60. If there are no pairs the script reports not_computable.

predictions.experiment: The same pooled within-problem concordance for the RL model.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows whose score_v3 is null/missing. Group by problem_index. Within each problem, form every pair (i, j) with score_v3_i == 1 and score_v3_j == 0. Pair value: 1 if n_new_j > n_new_i, 0.5 if n_new_j == n_new_i, 0 otherwise. Statistic = sum of pair values over all problems / total number of pairs over all problems. Problems with no such pair contribute nothing.
predictions.note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (committed). Same code as p1 with the RL file: 2,000 attempt-0 rows, no duplicate keys, score_v3 never null. Main ties = 0.5; alt_measured ties = 0 (the experiment's 'more new tokens' wording). RL has few wrong finished samples on MATH-500, so the pair count may be small and the fraction noisy; pooled pairs weight problems by (#right x #wrong). refuted_by: measured > 0.68.

predictions.experiment: Mean within-problem Spearman correlation of n_new with score_v3 for the cued base, over problems whose finished attempt-0 samples include at least one right and one wrong.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows with null/missing score_v3. Group by problem_index; keep problems with at least one row with score_v3 == 1 and at least one with score_v3 == 0. For each kept problem compute the Spearman rank correlation between n_new and score_v3 over its kept rows (ties get average ranks; skip a problem if all its n_new are equal). Statistic = unweighted mean of the per-problem correlations.
predictions.note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Mixed-problem filter is applied after dropping cap hits and later attempts (literal reading, matches 'finished attempt-0 samples' in the experiment). Spearman = Pearson on average ranks of n_new and of score_v3 (score ties get average ranks too). Problems with all n_new equal are skipped as written. Main = unweighted mean over problems; alt_measured = mean weighted by number of kept rows per problem (2-4), the most plausible other reading of 'mean'. With 2-4 rows per problem the per-problem rho takes few discrete values (e.g. +/-1 for 2 rows), so the mean is coarse. refuted_by: measured > -0.19.
